question: Goku is the spiky-haired hero of which manga and anime franchise created by Akira Toriyama in 1984?
context: Toriyama loosely based Goku on Sun Wukong from the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West. Goku's surname Son and the magical staff he carries early on come straight from that source.

question: In Dragon Ball Z, Goku's signature blue energy attack — fired with cupped hands and a long shouted name — is called what?
context: Goku learns the Kamehameha by watching Master Roshi perform it once. Toriyama's wife came up with the name, riffing on the Hawaiian king Kamehameha I.

question: What Studio Ghibli film features a fluffy gray forest spirit and a giant smiling Catbus that ferries two sisters through the countryside?
context: Released in 1988 alongside Takahata's Grave of the Fireflies as a double feature. Hayao Miyazaki wrote and directed it. The Totoro silhouette became the studio's logo.

question: Which 2001 Studio Ghibli film about a girl named Chihiro working in a bathhouse for spirits won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature?
context: Spirited Away won the Oscar at the 2003 ceremony. It also won the Golden Bear at Berlin, the only hand-drawn film ever to do so. Hayao Miyazaki did not attend the Oscars in protest of the Iraq War.

question: In Studio Ghibli's 1989 film, a young witch with a black cat named Jiji moves to a seaside town and starts a flying delivery service on her broomstick. What is the witch's name?
context: Kiki's Delivery Service was Miyazaki's first major box-office success in Japan. It was adapted from a children's novel by Eiko Kadono. The Japanese dub of Jiji has the cat speaking; the English dub kept him speaking throughout.

question: Lupin III is a master thief in a red or green jacket whose grandfather is the famous French gentleman-burglar from a series of novels. Which famous fictional thief is Lupin III's grandfather?
context: Monkey Punch created the manga in 1967. Arsene Lupin was the protagonist of stories by French author Maurice Leblanc starting in 1905. The Lupin estate periodically objected to the unauthorized grandson; the conflict shaped how Lupin III was credited overseas.

question: Astro Boy is a robot boy with rocket boots and laser fingers created by which Japanese cartoonist often called the godfather of manga?
context: Tezuka's Mighty Atom — Astro Boy in English — debuted in manga form in 1952. The 1963 TV anime adaptation was the first weekly half-hour animated television series in Japan. Tezuka also created Phoenix, Buddha, and Black Jack.

question: Sailor Moon's civilian name is Usagi Tsukino, and her group of Sailor Guardians are each named for a different planet. Who created the Sailor Moon manga in 1991?
context: Usagi means rabbit; the moon is associated with rabbits in Japanese folklore. The manga ran in Nakayoshi magazine. The 1992 Toei anime adaptation aired internationally and is the show most Western fans grew up with.

question: Which long-running anime franchise begun in 1996 features a teenage boy named Yugi Mutou and a card game his grandfather sells at his Domino City game shop?
context: Kazuki Takahashi created the manga in Weekly Shonen Jump. The Duel Monsters card game in the manga was so popular Konami launched the real-world Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game in 1999. Takahashi died in 2022 in a snorkeling accident off Okinawa.

question: Rumiko Takahashi's 1996 manga about a half-dog-demon and a modern-day schoolgirl who falls through a well into Sengoku-era Japan is called what?
context: Takahashi is one of the best-selling manga authors of all time. Inuyasha ran in Weekly Shonen Sunday from 1996 to 2008. Kagome Higurashi is the schoolgirl; Inuyasha is the half-demon she ends up shard-hunting with.

question: In Cowboy Bebop, the bounty-hunting crew of the Bebop spaceship includes Spike Spiegel, Jet Black, Faye Valentine, a hacker named Ed, and a Welsh Corgi named what?
context: Ein is a data dog — a genetically enhanced Pembroke Welsh Corgi smarter than most humans. Cowboy Bebop aired on TV Tokyo in 1998. Shinichiro Watanabe directed it and Yoko Kanno scored it with her band The Seatbelts.

question: Neon Genesis Evangelion centers on teenage pilots in giant biomechanical mechs fighting alien beings the show calls what?
context: Each Angel is named after a Judeo-Christian angel — Sachiel, Shamshel, Ramiel, Israfel, Sandalphon. The series aired on TV Tokyo from October 1995 to March 1996 and was created by Hideaki Anno at studio Gainax.

question: Released in 1988 by Tokyo Movie Shinsha, this animated film opens with a nuclear explosion over Tokyo in 1988 and jumps to 2019 Neo-Tokyo, where a teenage biker gang member named Tetsuo gains terrifying psychic powers. Who directed the film, adapting his own manga?
context: Akira's $11 million budget was the highest in anime history at that point. The manga began in Young Magazine in 1982 and continued until 1990; Otomo released the film midway through and altered the manga's ending afterward.

question: Ghost in the Shell, the 1995 animated film about cybernetic police major Motoko Kusanagi chasing a hacker called the Puppet Master, was directed by which filmmaker working from Masamune Shirow's manga?
context: Oshii had previously directed Patlabor. The Wachowskis showed Ghost in the Shell to producer Joel Silver as visual reference when pitching The Matrix. Shirow's manga began in Young Magazine in 1989.

question: Cowboy Bebop's iconic opening title sequence features a brassy big-band jazz number played by Yoko Kanno's band The Seatbelts over silhouetted characters and cards labeled with the crew's names. What is the opening song called?
context: Tank! is built around a walking bass riff and a horn line that became one of the most-recognized anime themes of all time. Kanno wrote dozens of pieces for the show; the soundtrack was released across four CD volumes plus a film score.

question: Studio Ghibli was founded in 1985 by Hayao Miyazaki, producer Toshio Suzuki, and which other director who would go on to make Grave of the Fireflies and Only Yesterday?
context: Takahata had been Miyazaki's mentor at Toei Animation. The studio name Ghibli comes from an Italian word for a hot Saharan wind — also the name of an Italian World War II scout plane that Miyazaki, an aviation enthusiast, admired.

question: Princess Mononoke, Miyazaki's 1997 film about a wolf-raised girl named San and a young Emishi prince cursed by a boar-god, broke Japanese box office records before being topped by which 1997 American film?
context: Mononoke was Japan's highest-grossing domestic film until Spirited Away topped it in 2001. Miramax bought the US distribution and Harvey Weinstein famously got told by producer Toshio Suzuki to stop demanding cuts — Suzuki sent him a katana with the message NO CUTS.

question: Rurouni Kenshin, Nobuhiro Watsuki's 1994 manga set in early Meiji-era Japan, follows a wandering swordsman who carries a katana with the blade and edge reversed so he cannot kill. What is this type of sword called in Japanese?
context: Sakabato means reverse-blade sword. Kenshin Himura was once the legendary Hitokiri Battosai assassin of the Bakumatsu period. Watsuki later landed in legal trouble in Japan that disrupted the manga's late run.

question: Trigun, Yasuhiro Nightow's 1995 manga turned 1998 anime, follows a gunfighter named Vash the Stampede across a desert planet. How much is the bounty on his head, the figure that opens every episode?
context: Vash is nicknamed the Humanoid Typhoon for the devastation that seems to follow him, though he himself refuses to kill. Studio Orange remade the series as Trigun Stampede in 2023 with full-CG animation.

question: Slayers, the 1995 anime adapted from Hajime Kanzaka's 1989 light novels, follows a red-haired teenage sorceress who casts a massively destructive black magic spell. What is the spell called?
context: Lina Inverse is the sorceress; she can also cast the even more dangerous Giga Slave, which draws from the Lord of Nightmares. Her party includes swordsman Gourry Gabriev, chimera Zelgadis Greywords, and princess Amelia Wil Tesla Saillune.

question: Mobile Suit Gundam, the original 1979 series that launched the Universal Century timeline and the entire real-robot genre, was created by which director who became the franchise's signature voice?
context: The original series was a ratings flop until reruns and the model kits — Gunpla — turned it into a juggernaut. Tomino is nicknamed Kill 'Em All Tomino for the body counts in his series. Wing in 1995 was the franchise's US Toonami breakthrough.

question: In Dragon Ball Z, the muscular green-skinned alien warrior who arrives on Earth at the start of the series, introduces the concept of Saiyans, and is Goku's older brother is named what?
context: Raditz arrives looking for his brother Kakarot — Goku's birth name. Goku and Piccolo team up to defeat him at the cost of Goku's life. Raditz reports back to Vegeta and Nappa before he dies, setting up the Saiyan saga.

question: Inuyasha, Ranma 1/2, and Urusei Yatsura were all written by Rumiko Takahashi, one of Japan's best-selling manga authors. Which 1978 series about an alien tiger-bikini-clad princess named Lum was her first major hit?
context: Urusei Yatsura ran in Weekly Shonen Sunday from 1978 to 1987. The title is a pun roughly meaning Those Obnoxious Aliens. Lum's catchphrase darling and her electric shocks became cultural touchstones in Japan.

question: Slam Dunk, the 1990 Takehiko Inoue manga that drove a Japanese basketball boom, follows a redheaded delinquent named Hanamichi Sakuragi who joins his high school team to impress a girl. What is the name of his high school in the series?
context: Inoue is now also famous for Vagabond, the Musashi Miyamoto epic. Slam Dunk is credited with inspiring a generation of Japanese basketball players. Inoue directed The First Slam Dunk, a 2022 animated theatrical film he wrote and storyboarded himself.

question: In Studio Ghibli's 1986 film about a girl named Sheeta who falls from the sky into the arms of a young miner named Pazu, the pair search for a legendary flying island bearing what name?
context: Castle in the Sky, also released as Laputa: Castle in the Sky, was the first official Studio Ghibli film. Miyazaki took the name from Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels. The film's sky pirates are led by the formidable matriarch Dola.

question: Berserk, the dark fantasy manga begun in 1988, follows a hulking mercenary swordsman who wields a massive iron sword and is hunted by demons. What is the swordsman's name?
context: Kentaro Miura drew Berserk in Young Animal magazine for over 30 years. Miura died unexpectedly in May 2021 at age 54. The manga has continued since 2022 under his longtime friend Kouji Mori and Studio Gaga.

question: Captain Tsubasa, the 1981 Yoichi Takahashi manga that inspired countless real-world soccer players, follows the rise of a young player named Tsubasa Ozora. What sport does the manga focus on?
context: Players including Lionel Messi, Andres Iniesta, Alessandro Del Piero, and Fernando Torres have all cited Captain Tsubasa as a childhood inspiration. The series ran in Weekly Shonen Jump.

question: Fist of the North Star, the 1983 manga set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland, features a martial artist who strikes opponents on hidden pressure points causing them to explode seconds later. What is his name?
context: Buronson wrote it and Tetsuo Hara drew it. The catchphrase you are already dead — omae wa mou shindeiru — became one of the most-quoted lines in anime. Kenshiro is the successor of the assassination art Hokuto Shinken.

question: Hayao Miyazaki's 1984 pre-Ghibli film about a windrider princess in a post-apocalyptic world of toxic jungles and giant insects is named for its heroine. What is her name?
context: Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind was based on Miyazaki's own manga, which he had begun in 1982. The film's commercial success was what made Studio Ghibli's founding in 1985 possible.

question: In Code Geass, the 2006 Sunrise series about an exiled prince leading a rebellion against the Holy Britannian Empire, the protagonist gains a power called Geass through a contract with a green-haired immortal girl. What is the prince's name?
context: C.C. is the immortal who grants Lelouch his Geass — the power of absolute obedience in anyone who meets his eyes. Lelouch's masked alter ego is Zero. Goro Taniguchi directed; Ichiro Okouchi wrote the scripts.

question: FLCL, the six-episode 2000 OVA co-produced by Gainax and Production I.G, opens with a Vespa-riding alien girl smacking a 12-year-old boy in the head with a bass guitar. What is her name?
context: Haruhara Haruko is the chaos that breaks open the everyday life of Naota Nandaba. FLCL — Fooly Cooly — was directed by Kazuya Tsurumaki. The soundtrack by the rock band The Pillows became iconic on its own.

question: Samurai Champloo, the 2004 Shinichiro Watanabe series, mashes Edo Japan with hip-hop. Fuu the waitress recruits two warring swordsmen to help her find a samurai with what unique trait?
context: Mugen is the wild swordsman; Jin is the stoic ronin; Fuu is the teenage waitress who recruited them. Nujabes provided much of the score, including Battlecry. The series ran 26 episodes on Fuji TV.

question: In Mushishi, the contemplative anime adaptation of Yuki Urushibara's 1999 manga, the wandering protagonist Ginko studies and treats people afflicted by supernatural creatures called what?
context: Mushi are primordial life forms — neither plant nor animal, neither benevolent nor malevolent. Ginko has white hair and a green eye because of his own encounter with them. Hiroshi Nagahama directed the 2005 anime.

question: Akira Toriyama's first major hit before Dragon Ball was a 1980 comedy manga about a little robot girl in glasses built by an inventor in Penguin Village. What is the manga called?
context: Arale Norimaki is the robot girl; Senbei Norimaki is her inventor. The manga ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 1980 to 1984. Toriyama later included Penguin Village cameos in Dragon Ball.

question: The Castle of Cagliostro, the 1979 animated film about Lupin III breaking into a small European principality to rescue Princess Clarisse, was the directorial feature debut of which animator?
context: Cagliostro is widely considered the best Lupin III film. Miyazaki had directed TV episodes before but this was his first theatrical feature. Steven Spielberg reportedly cited Cagliostro's car chase as among the greatest action sequences he had ever seen.

question: Digimon, the 1999 anime franchise about kids befriending digital monsters and adventuring in a Digital World, came from a Japanese toy line of virtual-pet keychains that competed with which other 1990s digital-pet toy?
context: Bandai released the original Digital Monster virtual pet in 1997, designed by Aki Maita's husband Akiyoshi Hongo as a boys' version of Tamagotchi. The Digimon Adventure anime introduced characters like Tai, Agumon, and Matt.

question: In Dragon Ball Z's Frieza saga on the planet Namek, Goku achieves a long-foretold transformation that turns his hair golden and his eyes green after Frieza murders his best friend Krillin. What is the name of this transformation?
context: Goku is the first Saiyan to achieve the form in over a thousand years. The transformation became one of the most-referenced moments in anime history. The Frieza arc on Namek famously lasted dozens of episodes despite the in-universe planet exploding in five minutes.

question: Neon Genesis Evangelion's three teenage pilots are Shinji Ikari, who pilots Eva Unit 01; the cheerful redheaded Asuka Langley Soryu, who pilots Eva Unit 02; and a quiet, pale girl who pilots Eva Unit 00. What is her name?
context: Rei has blue hair and red eyes and a flat affect — at least early in the series. Character designs were by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto, who also drew the manga adaptation. Rei's quiet presence and visual design became wildly influential on subsequent anime.

question: Studio Ghibli's 1992 film about a World War I flying ace turned bounty hunter in the Adriatic who has been cursed into the form of an anthropomorphic pig is called what?
context: Marco Pagot was the human pilot before the curse; Porco Rosso means Red Pig in Italian. Miyazaki, an aviation obsessive, drew the planes himself. The film originated as an in-flight short for Japan Airlines that grew into a feature.

question: In Akira, the teenage biker gang member who gains catastrophic psychic powers after a road accident and a government experiment is named Tetsuo. What is the name of his best friend and gang leader who tries to stop him?
context: Shotaro Kaneda rides the iconic red motorcycle whose long sliding stop became an instant cinema-shorthand for cyberpunk anime. The slide was hand-animated frame by frame. Mitsuo Iwata voiced Kaneda in Japanese; Cam Clarke voiced him in the original Streamline dub.

question: Funimation's English dub of Dragon Ball Z, which aired on Cartoon Network's Toonami in 1998, became iconic for two voice actors: Sean Schemmel voiced Goku, and the entire Vegeta-Piccolo-Yamcha-Roshi roster of male villain leads was largely voiced by which actor?
context: Sabat voices Vegeta, Piccolo, Yamcha, Mr. Popo, Burter, Recoome, Korin, Shenron, King Vegeta, and dozens of others. Schemmel voices Goku, Goten, King Kai, and Nail. Both actors started at Funimation in Texas and continued the roles for decades.

question: Studio Ghibli's 2013 film, which Miyazaki initially said would be his last theatrical feature, was a fictionalized biography of Jiro Horikoshi, the aeronautical engineer who designed the Mitsubishi A6M Zero fighter for the Imperial Japanese Navy. What is the film called?
context: The title comes from a line by Paul Valery quoted in a Tatsuo Hori novel: Le vent se leve, il faut tenter de vivre. Miyazaki returned from retirement in 2016 to direct The Boy and the Heron, which won the 2024 Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

question: The Eclipse — the apocalyptic event near the end of Berserk's Golden Age arc — is triggered when the imprisoned and crippled Griffith uses a crimson stone called what to make a contract with five godlike beings?
context: The Behelit is sometimes called the Egg of the King. The five beings Griffith contracts are the God Hand. Kentaro Miura drew the Eclipse arc as some of the most intense art in manga history; he kept refining the panels long afterward.

question: Cowboy Bebop's 26-episode run on TV Tokyo in 1998-1999 ends with its bounty-hunter protagonist Spike Spiegel walking back into the Red Dragon Syndicate's headquarters for one final confrontation. What is the name of the final episode?
context: The series was originally planned for 26 episodes but several stations only aired 13. The full run aired in Japan via WOWOW satellite. The 2001 theatrical film Knockin' on Heaven's Door is set between episodes 22 and 23 of the series.

question: Lupin III's lifelong rival and shadow is a perpetually exhausted ICPO Interpol inspector who has chased the thief across decades of stories. What is his name?
context: Koichi Zenigata is named for Heiji Zenigata, a fictional Edo-period police detective. The Castle of Cagliostro gave Zenigata the dignity of being the moral heart of Miyazaki's Lupin film. He has been voiced in Japanese by Goro Naya, Kiyoshi Kobayashi, and others.

question: Mobile Suit Gundam Wing, the 1995 series that became Toonami's breakout 2000 hit in the US, follows five teenage pilots from the L1 through L5 colonies sent to Earth in advanced mobile suits during AC 195. How many pilots are there?
context: The five Gundam pilots are Heero Yuy, Duo Maxwell, Trowa Barton, Quatre Raberba Winner, and Chang Wufei. Wing aired in the US on Cartoon Network's Toonami in March 2000 and ran as the kick-off to that block's anime mainstreaming.

question: Studio Ghibli's 2008 film about a five-year-old boy who keeps a magical fish-girl in a bucket on the seashore was directed by Hayao Miyazaki and inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's The Little Mermaid. What is the fish-girl's name?
context: Sosuke is the boy. Ponyo is the daughter of the sea-wizard Fujimoto and the sea-goddess Granmamare. Miyazaki personally hand-drew the film's distinctive wave sequences and reportedly threw out CGI experiments to keep the animation hand-drawn throughout.

question: Howl's Moving Castle, Miyazaki's 2004 film adapted from Diana Wynne Jones's 1986 novel, follows a young hat-maker named Sophie who is transformed into an old woman by a witch and takes refuge in a walking castle. What is the name of the castle's fire demon, who agreed to a contract with Howl?
context: Calcifer powers the castle by burning Howl's heart. Sophie's curse can be broken if she breaks the contract. Christian Bale voiced Howl and Billy Crystal voiced Calcifer in the English dub. Miyazaki took the directing job over from Mamoru Hosoda after the latter departed the project.

question: In Dragon Ball Z's Cell saga, the bio-android Cell achieves his perfect form by absorbing Android 17 and Android 18 — both products of the late Dr. Gero's lab. The arc climaxes at a tournament called the Cell Games, where a teenage Saiyan-hybrid named Gohan ascends to a new transformation by witnessing his father Goku sacrifice himself. What is Gohan's new transformation called?
context: Super Saiyan 2 was the first transformation beyond the original Super Saiyan ever shown. Gohan kills Cell with a one-armed father-son Kamehameha after his arm is broken. Funimation's English dub of the Cell Games arc aired on Cartoon Network in 1999 and became cultural shorthand for Gohan's potential.

question: Hideaki Anno founded studio Gainax in 1984 from a group of college friends who had produced the opening animation for the 1981 Daicon III science-fiction convention. Eva premiered on TV Tokyo on October 4, 1995. Anno was famously suffering from severe depression during production. The series's heavy use of Judeo-Christian symbolism — Sephiroth Tree, angels, Lance of Longinus — was chosen by Anno for what reason?
answer: Because it looked cool and was visually distinct from typical Japanese motifs
choices: Because it looked cool and was visually distinct from typical Japanese motifs
Because Anno had been studying Christian theology at Tokyo University seminary
Because the studio's American distributor required Western religious imagery
Because Gainax founder Toshio Okada was a devout Catholic theologian
context: Anno has repeatedly said in interviews that he and the staff found Christian imagery exotic and visually striking. The Tree of Life motif on the wall of NERV headquarters and the angel-name conventions are aesthetic choices, not statements of religious meaning. The Rebuild tetralogy began in 2007 and concluded in 2021 with Thrice Upon a Time.

question: Princess Mononoke's English dub, produced by Miramax in 1999, was written by which fantasy novelist, who fought with Harvey Weinstein over keeping the film's complexity intact?
context: Gaiman has said the experience was difficult — Weinstein wanted the dub simplified for American audiences. Producer Toshio Suzuki famously sent Weinstein a katana with the message NO CUTS. Billy Crudup voiced Ashitaka and Claire Danes voiced San.

question: Akira's score, composed by Tsutomu Ohashi under the collective name Geinoh Yamashirogumi, was unusual because it was recorded before most of the film was animated, then the visuals were cut to match the music. What three primary musical sources did Geinoh Yamashirogumi draw on for the score?
answer: Taiko drums, Indonesian gamelan, and traditional Japanese noh chanting
choices: Taiko drums, Indonesian gamelan, and traditional Japanese noh chanting
Synthesizer pads, jazz fusion, and Bulgarian women's choir
Traditional Chinese erhu, electronic ambient, and Korean folk drumming
Tibetan throat singing, sitar drones, and modern Tokyo street percussion
context: Ohashi's chorus was a real performing group composed of his university colleagues and amateur singers. The famous opening of the film — Kaneda's motorcycle headlight in the dark, then the title slamming on with the drums — was set to a piece called Kaneda from the score.

question: In Berserk's Golden Age arc, Guts is a battlefield mercenary recruited by the charismatic young commander of a mercenary company called the Band of the Hawk. The commander dreams of building his own kingdom and is loved by his swordswoman lieutenant Casca. What is the commander's name?
context: Griffith carries a small egg-like talisman called a Behelit. After his torture and crippling by the Midland king, he uses it to summon the God Hand in the Eclipse. Kentaro Miura drew the Golden Age arc across volumes 3 through 14 of the manga and considered it the manga's central story.

question: Yoko Kanno, the composer of Cowboy Bebop and many other anime scores, frequently fronts the studio band that performs the music live. The band's name is also a recurring inside joke — it shares its name with a safety device drivers should use. What is the band called?
context: The Seatbelts include guitarist Tsuneo Imahori and a roster of session players Kanno has worked with for decades. Kanno also scored Macross Plus, Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex, and Wolf's Rain. Her vocalist of choice for many Bebop tracks was Mai Yamane.

question: Castle in the Sky was originally going to be titled simply Laputa, but Disney's English distribution shortened the name for the 2003 dub release. Why was the original Spanish-derived word a problem?
answer: It is a vulgar Spanish slang word meaning a female prostitute
choices: It is a vulgar Spanish slang word meaning a female prostitute
It conflicted with a 1980s Italian fantasy film of similar title
It was the name of a Disney competitor's animated franchise
It triggered objections from Jonathan Swift's literary estate
context: Miyazaki took the name directly from Gulliver's Travels, where Swift apparently coined it without knowing the Spanish meaning. In Spanish-speaking countries the film has been released as El Castillo en el Cielo or Laputa: El Castillo en el Cielo despite the connotation.

question: Rurouni Kenshin's Kyoto arc, which many fans consider the series's high point, has the wandering swordsman Kenshin Himura travel to Kyoto to stop a master assassin who plans to overthrow the Meiji government with a private army. The antagonist's face is wrapped in bandages from burns covering most of his body. What is his name?
context: Shishio was Kenshin's successor as Hitokiri Battosai during the Bakumatsu. The Meiji government tried to assassinate him by setting him on fire. The Kyoto arc was adapted as a beautifully animated 1996-1998 TV arc and again in the 2014 live-action film Rurouni Kenshin: Kyoto Inferno starring Takeru Satoh.

question: In Dragon Ball Z's Majin Buu saga, the ancient sealed villain Buu first appears as a chubby pink child-like creature in a vest and white pantaloons. He befriends a blind boy and a dog and develops a sense of mercy before later transformations turn him into a sleeker, more violent form. What is the name of the blind boy who teaches Buu about kindness?
answer: Mr. Satan's friend, simply known as the blind boy in the manga
choices: Mr. Satan's friend, simply known as the blind boy in the manga
Bee, who appears later as Hercule Satan's loyal canine companion
Uub, who is later revealed to be the reincarnation of Kid Buu
Marron, the daughter of Krillin and Android 18, in a brief cameo
context: The fat form of Buu is the original sealed form. He splits into evil and good versions during the arc. The good Buu accompanies Mr. Satan into the Z-Fighters' final showdown. Toriyama's portrayal of the gentle fat Buu as the protagonist's ally became one of the manga's most emotionally resonant beats.

question: Dragon Ball Z Kai is a 2009 remastered version of DBZ that cut the original 291 episodes down to roughly 167 by removing filler and recutting pacing to closely follow Toriyama's manga. Which production company produced Kai under license from Toei?
answer: Toei Animation in-house, with new dubbing and a re-edit by Kazuhiro Furuhashi
choices: Toei Animation in-house, with new dubbing and a re-edit by Kazuhiro Furuhashi
Studio Pierrot, with new music by Yasuharu Takanashi and Konami sponsorship
Tokyo Movie Shinsha, with re-edits by Production I.G's Mamoru Oshii
Sunrise, with mecha-art consulting from Yoshiyuki Tomino and Bandai
context: Kai was originally aired in Japan from April 2009 to March 2011 and from 2014 to 2015 for the Buu saga. Funimation's English Kai dub featured most of the original DBZ cast — Sean Schemmel, Christopher Sabat, Sonny Strait — but tightened the dialogue and removed many of the original dub's added punchlines.

question: Mobile Suit Gundam's original 1979 series stars rookie pilot Amuro Ray, a teenager who stumbles into piloting a top-secret Federation mobile suit called the RX-78-2 Gundam during a Zeon attack. His rival across the series is a charismatic Zeon ace who wears a half-mask. What name does this rival go by?
context: Char's red mobile suit established the trope that ace pilots get a custom-colored unit three times faster than standard. His real name is Casval Rem Deikun. The Char-versus-Amuro rivalry runs through the original series, Zeta Gundam, Char's Counterattack, and decades of Universal Century continuity.

question: Princess Mononoke's wolf-raised protagonist San rides on the back of a massive white wolf-god who raised her. What is the wolf-god's name?
context: Moro is voiced in Japanese by actress Akihiro Miwa and in the English Miramax dub by Gillian Anderson. Okkoto is the elder boar-god. Lady Eboshi runs Irontown. Yakul is Ashitaka's loyal red elk. The film's eponymous mononoke is San herself — the wolf princess.

question: Trigun's gunfighter Vash the Stampede carries a customized .45-caliber long-barreled revolver, but the gun is actually a disguise for a different weapon-type built into his prosthetic arm by his brother. What kind of weapon is Vash's arm secretly equipped with?
context: Vash and his villain brother Knives are Plants — humanoid beings grown from the same biological-technology Plants that power the desert planet's cities. The angel arm appears late in the series. Yasuhiro Nightow's manga ran in Shonen Captain then Young King OURs from 1995 to 2008.

question: In Hayao Miyazaki's 1984 Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind, the titular princess flies a small one-seater glider through the toxic forest. What is her glider called?
context: Mehve comes from the German word Mowe, meaning seagull. The Mehve is jet-powered with a small engine slung beneath the wing. Studio Ghibli built a working flying replica in 2013 for engineering enthusiast Kazuhiko Hachiya's OpenSky project.

question: Studio Ghibli's 1988 film Grave of the Fireflies, directed by Isao Takahata, tells the story of two siblings struggling to survive in Kobe during the final months of World War II. The two main characters are a teenage boy and his much younger sister. What are their names?
context: Takahata adapted Akiyuki Nosaka's 1967 semi-autobiographical novel. Nosaka had lost his own younger sister to malnutrition during the war. The film was released as a double feature with Miyazaki's My Neighbor Totoro on April 16, 1988 — a contrast that astonished audiences.

question: Cowboy Bebop's hacker Edward Wong Hau Pepelu Tivrusky IV is a wild-haired child genius who joins the Bebop crew. Edward is referred to with which set of pronouns in the original Japanese, where the character's gender is deliberately ambiguous?
choices: Male, but with deliberately effeminate styling
Non-specified, kept ambiguous throughout the series
Different in different episodes for comedic effect
context: Edward is Ed for short. Aoi Tabuki voiced Ed in Japanese; Melissa Fahn voiced Ed in the English dub. Shinichiro Watanabe modeled the character on the daughter of a Yoko Kanno collaborator. Ed leaves the Bebop crew in episode 24 to find their father.

question: Toei Animation's 1980s Dragon Ball anime had distinctive opening songs that became cultural touchstones. The original Dragon Ball's opening theme was Makafushigi Adventure! The Z series, which began in 1989, opened with what now-iconic song?
context: Hironobu Kageyama performed Cha-La Head-Cha-La. The song was used as the opening for the first 199 episodes of DBZ. We Gotta Power was the second opening from episode 200 onward. Funimation's English dub replaced both with the famously rock-driven Rock the Dragon.

question: In Berserk, Guts wields a massive sword nearly as long as he is tall — a slab of iron forged to be obscenely large by a blacksmith called Godo. What is the name of Guts' signature sword?
context: Godo forged the sword for a king who wanted something a dragon could fall on. Guts takes the sword from Godo after losing his original weapon during the Eclipse. As the manga progresses, the Dragonslayer absorbs spiritual residue from the demons Guts kills and gains supernatural properties.

question: Ghost in the Shell's lead character Major Motoko Kusanagi is a fully cyberized human security operative working for which special-ops branch of Japan's national police?
context: Section 9 is run by Chief Aramaki, with Major Kusanagi as field commander and Batou as her second. Section 9 specializes in cyber-terrorism and corporate-political infiltration. Masamune Shirow's manga begins with Section 9 hunting the rogue hacker called the Puppeteer.

question: Slayers' Lina Inverse is a teenage sorceress whose appetite, temper, and willingness to flatten cities with the Dragon Slave have made her notorious across the Slayers world. What unflattering nickname does she earn that other characters frequently use to bait her?
context: Lina earns her reputation by ambushing and robbing bandit gangs as her main source of income. Her cup-size is a separate source of perpetual rage. Megumi Hayashibara voiced Lina Inverse for a decade across television, OVAs, films, and radio dramas. The Slayers franchise spans novels, manga, and multiple anime arcs.

question: Mushishi's protagonist Ginko is unique among the wandering mushishi — investigators of supernatural creatures — for one habit that he believes attracts mushi to him. What is this habit?
answer: He smokes constantly to suppress the mushi he naturally attracts
choices: He smokes constantly to suppress the mushi he naturally attracts
He carries iron talismans that ward off most mushi sightings
He drinks bitter tea to mask the scent that draws mushi to him
He wears only black clothing to make himself harder for mushi to see
context: Ginko's hair turned white and one eye became blind after an early encounter with mushi as a child. He travels from village to village treating mushi-related ailments and carries a wooden chest of mushi-related medicines. The 2005 anime adaptation by Artland is famously contemplative and atmospheric.

question: Lupin III's character ensemble centers on Lupin and three close associates: the sharpshooter Daisuke Jigen, the silent samurai Goemon Ishikawa XIII, and the femme fatale who alternates between rival and lover. What is the femme fatale's name?
context: Fujiko's name means mountain peak, a double-entendre noted by Monkey Punch in the manga's original 1967 run. Her motorcycle, her wardrobe, and her loyalty all shift on a per-heist basis. She has been voiced for decades by Eiko Masuyama, and after 2011 by Miyuki Sawashiro.

question: Studio Ghibli's 1991 film Only Yesterday, directed by Isao Takahata, was the first animated film selected for the official competition at the Cannes Film Festival, in 1991. The film follows a Tokyo office worker who takes a country vacation to a safflower farm and reflects on her fifth-grade self. What is the protagonist's adult name?
context: Takahata interleaves Taeko's adult vacation with flashbacks to her 1966 fifth-grade school year. The film is unusual for its quiet, slice-of-life tone. The English dub was produced by Disney in 2016 and features Daisy Ridley as adult Taeko.

question: In Code Geass, Lelouch vi Britannia receives his Geass power from C.C. in exchange for an unstated future contract. The visual signature of someone under Lelouch's Geass is a red sigil over the eye. What is the name of his shape-shifting masked vigilante alter-ego who leads the Black Knights resistance against Britannia?
context: Zero's mask conceals not only Lelouch's identity but the activation of his Geass. The Black Knights serve as the public face of the resistance against the occupation of Area 11, the former Japan. Goro Taniguchi directed; Ichiro Okouchi wrote the scripts; CLAMP did the character designs.

question: In March 1996, Neon Genesis Evangelion aired its final two episodes — 25 and 26 — to the famous fury of Japanese fans. The two episodes abandoned conventional storytelling entirely, instead consisting largely of internal monologues against minimal animation: pencil sketches, still frames, and black-screen white-text dialogue. Gainax was running out of both money and time, and Hideaki Anno chose to lean into psychological abstraction. In July 1997, Gainax released a full theatrical alternative ending. Earlier in March 1997, they had released a compilation film that mixed clips with the start of the new ending. What was that March 1997 film called?
context: Death and Rebirth's Death half was a clip-show recap; its Rebirth half was the first 27 minutes of what would become The End of Evangelion that July. Most Western releases bundled the two 1997 films together. The Rebuild tetralogy began with Evangelion 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone in 2007 and closed with Thrice Upon a Time in 2021.

question: Akira's 1988 production was so detailed it changed how anime was made. Otomo demanded that lip flaps be drawn precisely to the prerecorded Japanese voice tracks — the opposite of the industry standard at the time. The mouth movements visibly form Japanese vowels. The film used over 160,000 individual animation cels — more than double the typical anime feature of the era. What was the film's approximate production budget in US dollars?
context: 11 million 1988 US dollars was nearly twice the previous record for an anime production. The budget came largely from the Akira Committee — a consortium that included Bandai, Kodansha, Mainichi Broadcasting, Sumitomo Corporation, Toho, and Laserdisc Corporation. Kodansha's involvement was particularly aggressive because the manga had been their property for six years.

question: Ghost in the Shell's 1995 Mamoru Oshii feature contains a now-legendary sequence in which Major Kusanagi dives off a building roof and activates her thermoptic camouflage as she falls — disappearing visually against the Hong Kong-inspired city below. The cinematographer for the film, Hisao Shirai, used a custom multi-plane camera technique combined with what newer animation technology to achieve the layered depth?
answer: Computer graphics for compositing over hand-drawn cel animation
choices: Computer graphics for compositing over hand-drawn cel animation
Polarized light filters separating multiple hand-painted glass plates
Stop-motion 3D miniature sets photographed onto film with overlay paint
Reflective digital matte projection over hand-rotoscoped reference footage
context: Production I.G's compositing system was custom-built for the film. The Wachowskis screened Ghost in the Shell for The Matrix producer Joel Silver as a visual pitch reference. The opening titles sequence, in which Kusanagi's body is assembled from cybernetic components, was created with a similar mix of digital compositing and traditional cel animation.

question: Cowboy Bebop's bounty-hunter protagonist Spike Spiegel is a former member of the Red Dragon Syndicate's elite assassin unit. He fakes his own death and abandons the syndicate before the series begins, but his old crime-boss colleague — and the woman they both loved — pull him back in by the series's end. What is the name of Spike's former colleague and rival?
context: Vicious is voiced by Norio Wakamoto in Japanese and Skip Stellrecht in the original English dub. Julia is the woman they both loved. The flashback episode Ballad of Fallen Angels in episode 5 is the series's first glimpse of Vicious. Episodes 25 and 26 — The Real Folk Blues — close the Vicious arc and end the series.

question: Hayao Miyazaki had publicly retired from feature direction at least seven times before his 2023 return with The Boy and the Heron, but the most-cited retirement came with which 2013 Ghibli film, which he stated at its Venice Film Festival premiere would be his final theatrical work?
context: The Wind Rises is a fictionalized biography of Jiro Horikoshi, the designer of the Mitsubishi A6M Zero. The film was politically controversial in Japan for its critical treatment of the wartime aircraft industry. Miyazaki broke retirement in 2016 to begin The Boy and the Heron, which won the 2024 Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.

question: Studio Ghibli's third theatrical film was a 1988 release directed by Isao Takahata, set in 1945 Kobe under American firebombing. Takahata adapted Akiyuki Nosaka's 1967 semi-autobiographical novella about losing his own younger sister to malnutrition. The film was released as a double feature with My Neighbor Totoro on April 16, 1988 — schoolchildren watched Totoro first, then sat through this devastating second feature. What was the film called?
context: The double feature ended audiences and reviewers alike. Takahata's film became one of the most-cited anti-war films in cinema history. Roger Ebert listed it on his Great Movies list. Takahata himself was personally opposed to wartime nostalgia and used the period setting to indict adult abandonment of children, not just American bombing.

question: Berserk's manga was first serialized in November 1989 in Hakusensha's Monthly Animal House, then moved to Young Animal magazine in 1992 where it ran for the rest of Kentaro Miura's life. Miura died of acute aortic dissection on May 6, 2021 at age 54. Volume 41, published posthumously, contained chapter 364 — the last chapter Miura himself completed. The manga has continued under Miura's longtime friend Kouji Mori and the assistants of which studio?
context: Mori is the author of the manga Holyland and a friend of Miura's since high school. He told the publisher Hakusensha that Miura had shared the full ending of Berserk with him in detail. Chapter 365, the first chapter under Mori's supervision, was published in Young Animal in June 2022.

question: The Mobile Suit Gundam franchise's iconic protagonist mobile suit — the RX-78-2 — was designed by which mechanical designer, who became the franchise's signature mecha artist for decades?
context: Okawara is widely considered the first dedicated mechanical designer in anime. He designed not only the original Gundam but the Zaku, the Dom, the Gouf, and the Zeong. Katoki took over much of the redesign work in the 1990s and 2000s. Tomino once said Okawara's designs were so dense with detail they made every model kit profitable.

question: Funimation's English dub of Dragon Ball Z, which began on Cartoon Network's Toonami block in August 1998, did not have one single longtime voice for Goku — three different actors played him over the years. Sean Schemmel was the longest-running; he replaced Peter Kelamis after a previous Saban-era dub. Who was the actor who first voiced Goku in the original 1996 Funimation Ocean-studio dub, distinguished by a deeper voice closer to the Japanese version's adult tone?
context: Ian Corlett actually voiced Goku in the 1996 Ocean dub; Kelamis took over partway through. Saffron Henderson voiced Goku in the original 1989 Saban Dragon Ball pilot. Brian Drummond is the Ocean studio's Vegeta — the original IT'S OVER 9000 actor. Schemmel auditioned for Goku at Funimation in 1999 and held the role into the 2020s.

question: Princess Mononoke's English dub was overseen by Miramax in 1999. Producer Toshio Suzuki famously responded to demands from Harvey Weinstein for narrative cuts by sending him a katana with a single message attached. What was the message?
context: The story has been confirmed by Suzuki himself in interviews. Mononoke was released theatrically in 1999 in the US through Miramax. Neil Gaiman wrote the English dub script. Billy Crudup voiced Ashitaka. Claire Danes voiced San. Minnie Driver voiced Lady Eboshi. Gillian Anderson voiced the wolf-god Moro.

question: Rurouni Kenshin's 2012 live-action film was directed by Keishi Otomo and starred Takeru Satoh as Kenshin Himura. The film and its 2014 sequels became some of the highest-grossing live-action manga adaptations in Japanese cinema. Satoh trained for over a year in real iaijutsu sword techniques to perform the role's swordplay. The 2014 sequel covered the manga's most-beloved arc. What was the sequel called?
context: Kyoto Inferno was followed by The Legend Ends later in 2014 — the two films together adapt the Kyoto arc. Satoh later returned for The Final and The Beginning, the 2021 two-part conclusion covering the Jinchu arc and Kenshin's Bakumatsu past. Satoh's casting is now widely cited as the gold standard for live-action manga adaptation.

question: Cowboy Bebop's score by Yoko Kanno is famously jazz-fusion and big-band influenced. Kanno's band The Seatbelts recorded many tracks live in the studio with vocalist Mai Yamane. The opening theme Tank! is performed in a distinct big-band style with which lead instrument carrying the iconic theme melody?
context: Tsuneo Imahori plays the show's guitar lines. The walking bass that drives Tank! is played by Saburo Suzuki. Kanno conducts and plays keyboard. The show used roughly 80 distinct compositions across its short run. The Bebop's brass-band aesthetic was designed to clash with the show's spacefaring cyberpunk setting.

question: Spirited Away's Yubaba — the witch who runs the bathhouse and steals Chihiro's name — has an identical twin sister who lives in a swamp cottage on a distant rail line and represents Yubaba's gentler shadow. What is the twin's name?
context: Yubaba and Zeniba together represent two halves of one being in Miyazaki's design — they have the same face but opposite temperaments. The train trip to Zeniba's cottage in the swamp is one of the film's most-praised sequences. Both are voiced in Japanese by veteran actress Mari Natsuki.

question: Lupin III: The Castle of Cagliostro features a now-legendary car chase early in the film: Lupin, fleeing in a tiny yellow Fiat 500, leaps from a winding mountain road across the gap to a sheer cliff face, runs the car up the wall using sheer momentum, and lands on a higher road. The animation was directed by which animator, working under Miyazaki?
answer: Hayao Miyazaki himself drew the key animation for the sequence
choices: Hayao Miyazaki himself drew the key animation for the sequence
Yasuo Otsuka, who animated most of the rest of the film
Takeshi Honda, an early career credit at Telecom Animation
Yoshifumi Kondo, who later directed Whisper of the Heart
context: Yasuo Otsuka was the animation director on Cagliostro overall and Miyazaki's mentor at Toei. Miyazaki personally drew several of the film's signature action sequences. Steven Spielberg reportedly told a Telecom Animation visitor that the car chase was the greatest he had ever seen in any medium.

question: Slayers' Lina Inverse is voiced by Megumi Hayashibara, one of the most prolific voice actresses in anime history. Hayashibara is also famous for voicing what other 1990s anime protagonist — a quiet, emotionally-suppressed Eva pilot with blue hair and red eyes?
answer: Rei Ayanami in Neon Genesis Evangelion
choices: Rei Ayanami in Neon Genesis Evangelion
Misato Katsuragi in Neon Genesis Evangelion
Asuka Langley Soryu in Neon Genesis Evangelion
context: Hayashibara also voiced Ranma Saotome's female form in Ranma 1/2, Ai Haibara in Detective Conan, Atsuko Natsume in All Purpose Cultural Cat Girl Nuku Nuku, and Pikachu's pre-Pokemon ancestor in Pokemon (the female Pikachu was Ikue Otani). Hayashibara is also a J-pop singer who has performed dozens of anime theme songs.

question: Yoshiyuki Sadamoto designed the characters for Neon Genesis Evangelion and was a Gainax veteran from the Daicon III convention animation in 1981. Sadamoto's published manga adaptation of Eva took how many years to complete after the anime ended?
answer: Roughly fourteen years, finishing in June 2013
choices: Roughly fourteen years, finishing in June 2013
Roughly seven years, finishing in late 2003
context: Sadamoto began the manga in 1994 ahead of the anime's broadcast. Volume 14 — the final volume — was published in June 2013. The manga's ending diverges significantly from both the original TV series and End of Evangelion. Sadamoto also did character designs for FLCL, The Wings of Honneamise, and Summer Wars.

question: Astro Boy was Osamu Tezuka's most famous creation, but Tezuka is also credited with founding the conventions of modern manga storytelling: cinematic paneling, big-eyed character design, and serial story structure. Tezuka had originally trained in what profession before becoming a full-time cartoonist?
answer: Medicine, earning his medical degree and license
choices: Medicine, earning his medical degree and license
Engineering, with a focus on radio electronics
Architecture, having designed two buildings in Osaka
Law, briefly practicing in Tokyo before his first manga sale
context: Tezuka qualified as a medical doctor at Osaka University before deciding cartooning was his calling. His medical training shaped Black Jack — the long-running manga about a brilliant unlicensed surgeon. Tezuka founded the animation studio Mushi Production in 1961 to produce Astro Boy and later Princess Knight and Kimba the White Lion.

question: Hayao Miyazaki famously hand-paints storyboards as he directs, often beginning a film without a finished script. For one Ghibli feature, he is known to have begun production with only the first 30 percent of the story plotted, then improvised the rest as animation proceeded. Which film's production followed this notoriously freewheeling process?
context: Miyazaki has said in multiple interviews that he started Spirited Away with the daughter-of-a-family-friend pitch — a ten-year-old girl who needed a film made for her — and worked out where the bathhouse story would go as he drew it. The production overran budget and time but became the highest-grossing Japanese film ever upon release.

question: Cowboy Bebop's intentional 26-episode count and big-band style were both influenced by Shinichiro Watanabe's pitch document, which framed the show as a love letter to which two cinematic genres of mid-twentieth-century America?
choices: Screwball comedy and the gangster picture
Hard-boiled detective and the war film
Pulp adventure and the Bogart vehicle
context: Watanabe's pitch leaned hard on bringing American jazz-era and western cinematic conventions to a spacefaring future. The bounty-hunter setup is straight from western tradition. The character of Spike is consciously modeled on Bruce Lee and 1970s Hong Kong cinema. The show's title combines cowboy with bebop jazz.

question: Berserk's Eclipse — the cataclysmic event closing the Golden Age arc — is precipitated when Griffith, having been imprisoned and tortured into permanent crippling, uses the Behelit to summon the God Hand. The God Hand offer him a contract: ascension to their ranks in exchange for the sacrifice of his entire mercenary company. Griffith accepts. How many members of the God Hand are there at the start of the Eclipse?
answer: Four, with Griffith being inducted as the fifth
choices: Four, with Griffith being inducted as the fifth
Five, with Griffith subordinated as the sixth
Three, with Griffith being inducted as the fourth
Seven, with Griffith being inducted as the eighth
context: The original four God Hand members are Void, Slan, Ubik, and Conrad. Griffith — reborn as Femto — joins as the fifth and youngest. The Eclipse occurs every 216 years; in Berserk it falls on the year of Griffith's beheliting. Miura drew the Eclipse arc across volumes 12 through 13 of the manga.

question: Mobile Suit Gundam Seed — the 2002 Sunrise series that revitalized the franchise for a new generation — was directed by Mitsuo Fukuda. The series's lead protagonist mobile suit was the GAT-X105 Strike Gundam, piloted by which conflicted teenage Coordinator pilot?
context: The series sets up a war between genetically engineered humans called Coordinators and natural-born humans called Naturals. Kira is a Coordinator raised among Naturals. The series spawned a 2004 sequel Gundam Seed Destiny and a long-delayed theatrical film Mobile Suit Gundam Seed Freedom in 2024.

question: Ghibli's distinctive style includes a great deal of food animation — Miyazaki has repeatedly said that depicting eating well is a moral act for an animator. Which Ghibli film features a celebrated cooking-bacon-and-eggs sequence that became a touchstone of food animation?
answer: Howl's Moving Castle, with Howl cooking breakfast for Sophie and Markl
choices: Howl's Moving Castle, with Howl cooking breakfast for Sophie and Markl
Spirited Away, with Chihiro's parents devouring spirit-food at the empty stall
Ponyo, with Sosuke's mother Lisa preparing ramen for Ponyo's first meal
My Neighbor Totoro, with Satsuki packing a bento for her little sister Mei
context: All four of these Ghibli food scenes are famously well-animated. Howl's bacon-and-eggs scene, with Calcifer crackling in the hearth and Howl flipping the pan, is the most-clipped of the four for animation studies. The Spirited Away spirit-food scene became iconic for the way the parents are transformed into pigs.

question: Trigun's manga ran in two distinct phases. The original 1995 manga in Tokuma Shoten's Shonen Captain ran for three volumes before the magazine folded. Yasuhiro Nightow continued the story in 1998 in a different magazine — Shogakukan's Young King OURs — under a new title that ran through 2007 across fourteen additional volumes. What was the continuation manga called?
context: Trigun Maximum runs to fourteen volumes plus a final volume often packaged separately. The 1998 anime adaptation by Madhouse only covers the original three-volume Trigun and improvises an ending. Studio Orange's 2023 Trigun Stampede is a full-CG reboot directed by Kenji Muto.

question: Lupin III has been voiced by multiple actors over decades. The longest-running voice — performing from 1979's Castle of Cagliostro through 2010's series — was a Japanese voice actor named Yasuo Yamada. After Yamada's death in 1995, the role passed to another voice actor whose performance is most associated with the long-running TV specials. Who took over the role after Yamada?
context: Kurita has voiced Lupin from 1995 onward in TV specials, films, and OVAs. Kobayashi was the longtime voice of Jigen. Inoue voiced Goemon. Naya voiced Inspector Zenigata. The mass cast-change in 2011 — the 40th-anniversary refresh — replaced Kobayashi, Inoue, Naya, and Masuyama in the same season, leaving Kurita as the sole holdover.

question: Akira's iconic motorcycle slide — the moment where Kaneda's red motorcycle is brought to a stop with a long perpendicular drift, sparks flying, accompanied by a slamming taiko drum — has been homaged in dozens of subsequent films, music videos, and video games over four decades, including Looper, Chronicle, Kanye West's Stronger video, the second Spider-Verse film, and Ready Player One. The motorcycle's distinctive jet-engine sound came from what real-world Japanese source recorded on location?
answer: A modified Kawasaki Ninja motorcycle, recorded on a closed Tokyo street
choices: A modified Kawasaki Ninja motorcycle, recorded on a closed Tokyo street
An actual jet engine test cell at the Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Komaki facility
A library recording from a 1976 Honda CB750 commercial overlaid with synth pulse
A custom-built piezo-electric resonance device by sound designer Tsuneo Imahori
context: The Kaneda bike is specifically based on a Norton Manx-inspired streamlined design with all-red painted bodywork. The bike has appeared as a real ride-able replica in multiple Akira anniversary exhibitions. The two-stroke jet-pulse sound effect was layered over heavy taiko drums by sound designer Susumu Hirasawa.

question: Cowboy Bebop's classic 26-episode run famously aired on TV Tokyo in 1998 in a heavily censored partial-run that skipped multiple episodes due to a real-world incident. After the 1998 partial run, the show aired in full on WOWOW from October 1998 to April 1999. The censor cuts were related to a particular Japanese national tragedy that the series's depictions of organized terror seemed too sensitive against. What real-world 1995 event made TV Tokyo balk at airing certain Bebop episodes?
answer: The Tokyo subway sarin gas attack by Aum Shinrikyo
choices: The Tokyo subway sarin gas attack by Aum Shinrikyo
The Great Hanshin Earthquake in Kobe in early January
The Sakaide-Marugame ferry sinking off the Inland Sea
The eruption of Mount Unzen on the Shimabara Peninsula
context: The Aum Shinrikyo attack on the Tokyo subway in March 1995 killed 13 people and injured thousands. TV Tokyo refused to air Bebop episodes featuring biological terror, network terror, or attacks on commuter trains. The full series aired only on WOWOW satellite later. Shinichiro Watanabe has discussed the censorship in subsequent interviews.

question: Hideaki Anno's choice of religious symbolism for Eva — angels named after Jewish-Christian angels, the Tree of Life on the wall of NERV headquarters, the Spear of Longinus, the Adam and Lilith first-being framework — has been widely studied. Anno has said in multiple interviews that he chose the symbols not for theological meaning but because they were aesthetically distinct from common Japanese motifs. The Sephiroth Tree image on the NERV wall was sourced from what specific Western esoteric work?
answer: Athanasius Kircher's 17th-century Oedipus Aegyptiacus illustration of the Sephirot
choices: Athanasius Kircher's 17th-century Oedipus Aegyptiacus illustration of the Sephirot
Eliphas Levi's 19th-century Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie diagrams
John Dee's 16th-century Enochian tables transcribed by Edward Kelley
Aleister Crowley's early 20th-century Book of Thoth tarot illustrations
context: Kircher was a 17th-century Jesuit polymath whose Oedipus Aegyptiacus is a baroque attempt to interpret Egyptian hieroglyphs through Kabbalistic Christianity. The Sephirot diagram from that book was widely reproduced in occultism textbooks and appears in the NERV command center. Anno's production team has confirmed the source in art-book interviews.

question: Spirited Away's iconic train sequence — Chihiro and No-Face riding a train across a flooded plain at dusk to reach Zeniba's cottage — was animated to a quiet score by Joe Hisaishi called One Summer's Day. Miyazaki specifically requested that the train have no destination announcements, only that it stop at specific stations whose names are visible on signs. The stations all have what feature in common?
answer: Each station's name is written in old-fashioned right-to-left Japanese on the platform signs
choices: Each station's name is written in old-fashioned right-to-left Japanese on the platform signs
Each station has been transliterated from real-world locations on the Hokkaido island rail network
Each station name corresponds to a different obsolete Japanese era name from the Edo period
Each station displays both its current name and the name it had before postwar romanization reform
context: Miyazaki insisted on the old right-to-left orthography to create the sense of a different era. The train cars themselves are reminiscent of pre-war Japanese coaches. The passengers are translucent black silhouettes — souls in transit. Hisaishi composed One Summer's Day on a single piano take that Miyazaki refused to let him re-record.

question: Dragon Ball Z's most-quoted English-dub line — Vegeta's shout that his scouter has detected Goku's power level — was actually a slight mistranslation of the original Japanese script. In the manga and Japanese anime, Vegeta's scouter actually reads what number?
answer: Eight thousand, with the meme number being a Funimation dub change
choices: Eight thousand, with the meme number being a Funimation dub change
Eleven thousand five hundred, which the dub rounded down
Twelve thousand, exactly as the dub stated in the line
Twenty-three thousand, before Vegeta's own training power-up
context: The Japanese line is hassen ijou da — over eight thousand. The Ocean Group's 1996 dub by writer Linda Young changed the line to over nine thousand because nine thousand has a more cartoonish ring. Brian Drummond's iconic delivery — IT'S OVER NINE THOUSAND — became one of the most-memed anime moments of all time. Schemmel and the later Funimation cast kept the dub's number for continuity.

question: Studio Ghibli is fiercely protective of its films's traditional hand-drawn animation. The studio resisted digital techniques for years, and Miyazaki was famously dismissive of a 2016 student demonstration of AI-driven animation, telling the audience that he felt the work was an insult to life itself. However, one specific Ghibli film did use computer-generated effects extensively — for a particular scene of an army-on-horseback charge. Which film was this?
answer: Princess Mononoke, for the demon-boar Nago and the catastrophic later boar charge
choices: Princess Mononoke, for the demon-boar Nago and the catastrophic later boar charge
Howl's Moving Castle, for the walking castle's eight chimney-leg mechanical assembly
Spirited Away, for the river-god's translucent watery body in the bathhouse scene
The Wind Rises, for the Mitsubishi Zero's three-axis aerodynamic test sequences
context: Princess Mononoke used Toyo Links's digital painting and compositing extensively. The boar Nago at the film's opening, the army of demonic boars later in the film, and the corrupted forest spirit's collapse all use computer-aided effects. Miyazaki was reportedly furious with the test sequences and demanded they be redone repeatedly until they looked hand-drawn.

question: Studio Ghibli's distinctive logo — a Totoro silhouette — was designed shortly after My Neighbor Totoro's 1988 release. The original Studio Ghibli pre-Totoro logo, used briefly during Castle in the Sky and Grave of the Fireflies production, was a simple typographic mark with no character. The Totoro silhouette adoption was a deliberate marketing decision driven by which Ghibli figure?
choices: Director Isao Takahata as a Totoro endorsement
Animator Yoshifumi Kondo, who designed the silhouette
context: Suzuki is the long-running producer behind nearly every Ghibli release. He had previously worked at Animage magazine before joining Ghibli. The Totoro silhouette became one of the most-recognizable production-company logos in cinema. Suzuki's decision was made over Miyazaki's initial objection that the choice would over-identify the studio with a single film.

question: Berserk's 1997 OVA adaptation, produced by OLM, covered the manga's Golden Age arc in 25 half-hour episodes. The opening theme song, performed by Susumu Hirasawa, became iconic on its own. The closing theme, also by Hirasawa, was titled with a distinct phrase from the manga's spiritual mythology. What was the closing theme called?
context: Susumu Hirasawa scored not only the 1997 OVA but also the 2012-2013 Berserk Golden Age films. Hirasawa's distinctive electronic-orchestral style — which he had developed for his band P-Model and his solo work — was uniquely suited to Berserk's grim tone. He also scored Satoshi Kon's Paranoia Agent and Millennium Actress.

question: Cowboy Bebop's lead character Spike Spiegel has a distinctive one-eye visual feature explained briefly in a flashback to his pre-series time with the Red Dragon Syndicate. His right eye is a cybernetic prosthetic, and Spike's running internal joke is that his right eye sees the present while his left eye sees the past. The flashback episode that explains this is named after which character?
answer: Episode 17, Mushroom Samba — though the eye is briefly referenced in the Ballad of Fallen Angels flashback
choices: Episode 17, Mushroom Samba — though the eye is briefly referenced in the Ballad of Fallen Angels flashback
Episode 5, Ballad of Fallen Angels — Spike's first flashback to Julia and Vicious
Episode 12, Jupiter Jazz Part 1 — Vicious's flashback to the Red Dragon training facility
Episode 26, The Real Folk Blues Part 2 — Spike's final return to the syndicate
context: Spike's cybernetic eye is mentioned across the series but never the centerpiece of a single episode. The Ballad of Fallen Angels flashback in episode 5 is the cleanest reference. Watanabe's pitch document for the series explicitly noted that Spike's two-eye dichotomy was a deliberate visual reference to noir cinema's split-perspective character framing.

question: Trigun's protagonist Vash the Stampede has a real-world Marshal Arts inspiration — the gunfighter's stance, the spinning revolver flourishes, the kicked-back hat, the long red coat — but the gun itself was modeled on a specific real-world prop firearm. Vash's customized .45-caliber revolver design was inspired by which actor's signature on-screen handgun?
answer: Clint Eastwood's gun from the Dollars trilogy — a Colt 1851 Navy conversion
choices: Clint Eastwood's gun from the Dollars trilogy — a Colt 1851 Navy conversion
Charles Bronson's gun from Once Upon a Time in the West — a Remington 1858 New Army
John Wayne's gun from The Searchers — a sawed-off Winchester Model 1873
Lee Van Cleef's gun from For a Few Dollars More — a Remington Rolling Block carbine
context: Yasuhiro Nightow has said Vash's whole visual presentation — including the coat, the hair, and the gun — was deliberately styled after spaghetti western cinema, especially the films of Sergio Leone. The 1998 anime adaptation by Madhouse leans even harder into the western framing than the manga does.

question: Lupin III: The Castle of Cagliostro's villain — Count Cagliostro — is named after a real 18th-century Italian occultist and counterfeiter. Hayao Miyazaki researched the historical figure for the film. What was the real Cagliostro famous for in 18th-century Europe?
answer: Posing as an alchemist and Freemason while running fraudulent diamond-and-elixir schemes across European courts
choices: Posing as an alchemist and Freemason while running fraudulent diamond-and-elixir schemes across European courts
