question: Mobile Suit Gundam's original 1979 series was a ratings disaster at first broadcast but achieved cultural-touchstone status through reruns and through the Gunpla model-kit phenomenon. What was the specific Bandai-published model-kit line — released starting July 1980 — that turned Gundam into a juggernaut?
answer: The 1/144 scale Gunpla series, starting with the RX-78-2 in plastic-snap form
choices: The 1/144 scale Gunpla series, starting with the RX-78-2 in plastic-snap form
The Action Mecha figure line, starting with a die-cast metal Zaku at 1/60 scale
The Imai die-cast Mecha Treasures series, building on Mobile Pod 79 designs
The Hasegawa Pro-Built series, premiering at Tokyo Hobby Show 1980 in February
context: The first Gunpla kits sold out within hours of their July 1980 release. The market quickly justified producing every mobile suit from the show as a kit. The Gunpla phenomenon — and the model-kit-driven anime industry it created — is now a multi-billion-dollar business. The 1981 Mobile Suit Gundam trilogy of theatrical recompilations brought the series to the wider Japanese audience.

question: Osamu Tezuka's lifelong influence on Hayao Miyazaki is well documented, but Miyazaki has publicly criticized Tezuka's animation work as overly commercial and rushed. Miyazaki has reserved particular praise for one Tezuka manga — a sprawling philosophical work begun in 1954 and worked on across decades. The work follows the immortal Phoenix and a series of reincarnating mortals across vastly different eras of human history. What is the work called?
answer: Hi no Tori, often translated as Phoenix
choices: Hi no Tori, often translated as Phoenix
Buddha, Tezuka's eight-volume biography of Siddhartha Gautama
Black Jack, the long-running surgeon-vigilante manga
Adolf, the World War II tri-track historical novel manga
context: Hi no Tori was Tezuka's self-described lifework. He began it in 1954 and continued working on it until his death in 1989. He never completed the planned final volume. The work jumps between ancient Japan, far-future space settlement, and meditations on memory and identity. Miyazaki has said in interviews that Hi no Tori is the manga he would have most wanted to direct as a feature film.

question: Princess Mononoke's English Miramax dub — written by Neil Gaiman and produced over Harvey Weinstein's objection — required Miyazaki to approve every casting choice. One Hollywood actor was personally requested by Miyazaki himself for a specific role: the ironworks-running, gun-slinging female lead. What actor was cast as Lady Eboshi at Miyazaki's personal request?
context: Driver has discussed in interviews that Miyazaki had seen her in Good Will Hunting and felt her voice carried the warmth and the steel he wanted in Eboshi. Billy Bob Thornton voiced Jigo. Billy Crudup voiced Ashitaka. Claire Danes voiced San. Gillian Anderson voiced Moro. The dub became one of the most-praised English dubs of any Ghibli release.

question: Rurouni Kenshin's 1996 anime adaptation by Studio Gallop and Studio Deen ran into a particularly distinctive problem during its third season. The animation studios diverged completely from Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga because Watsuki had not yet finished it. The third season — the Black Knight Squad arc — was written entirely as anime-original material under what now-common production constraint?
answer: The anime had caught up to the still-running manga, forcing original filler
choices: The anime had caught up to the still-running manga, forcing original filler
Watsuki had a contractual conflict with Shueisha over manga continuation rights
Studio Deen had a deal to produce an entirely original World War II historical arc
Fuji TV demanded an isekai-style transition arc for ratings in late-1990s primetime
context: The Black Knight Squad arc — sometimes called the Christian arc — is widely considered the series's weakest period. Long-running anime adaptations of ongoing manga famously face this problem; later examples include Naruto's Filler-Naruto arcs and Bleach's Bount arc. The 2012-2014 OVA Rurouni Kenshin: Tsuiokuhen and Seisouhen returned to faithful Watsuki adaptation.

question: Hayao Miyazaki has long been a critic of digital animation, but he made one striking exception for a 2008 film. Ponyo's distinctive flowing-wave animation was achieved with what unusual technique that Miyazaki personally pioneered for the film?
answer: All waves were hand-drawn frame by frame in colored pencil on paper, scanned and not digitally smoothed
choices: All waves were hand-drawn frame by frame in colored pencil on paper, scanned and not digitally smoothed
Each wave was rendered in custom-built fluid-dynamics software at Studio Ghibli
Stock-footage water reference plates were rotoscoped frame by frame into the animation
A motion-capture rig with water-tank reference was used to drive Toyo Links wave models
context: Ponyo's waves were a deliberate refusal of computer fluid simulation. Miyazaki has discussed in interviews that he wanted the waves to feel like living creatures, and that the only way to achieve that was hand-drawing every frame in colored pencil. The film required over 170,000 individual frames. Many were drawn by Miyazaki himself.

question: Dragon Ball's 1986 anime adaptation by Toei Animation famously took longer to tell the early Red Ribbon Army arc than Toriyama's manga did. The anime stretched the arc with original content. One particular long-running anime-original sequence — Goku's training under Korin to fight the Red Ribbon Army's elite assassin — featured a now-classic training device adapted from the manga. What was the device?
answer: The Sacred Water, which turns out to have been a Karin Tower trick to make Goku train
choices: The Sacred Water, which turns out to have been a Karin Tower trick to make Goku train
The Senzu Beans, dispensed by Korin only after the Red Ribbon arc concluded
The King Kai Gravity Chamber, introduced at the foot of Karin Tower for the assassin fight
The Hyperbolic Time Chamber, accessed early through Korin Tower for the Tao Pai Pai fight
context: Korin — Karin in some translations — is the white anthropomorphic cat sage who lives at the top of Korin Tower. He convinces Goku that drinking the Sacred Water will make him stronger; in fact, the training of repeatedly trying to take the water from Korin is what makes Goku strong enough to defeat Tao Pai Pai. The Senzu Beans are introduced later. The Hyperbolic Time Chamber is a Cell-saga element.

question: Cowboy Bebop's title sequence and its closing-credit roll famously use what design technique to convey the show's mid-century jazz-noir-western fusion identity?
answer: Saul Bass-inspired silhouetted figures against blocks of solid color, with hand-typeset character cards
choices: Saul Bass-inspired silhouetted figures against blocks of solid color, with hand-typeset character cards
Wong Kar-wai-inspired smeared neon long-exposure photography against handwritten kanji
Spike Lee-inspired multi-camera split-screen with stenciled industrial-magazine typography
Andy Warhol-inspired repeated portrait grids with Letraset-printed character introductions
context: Saul Bass designed title sequences for Hitchcock, Preminger, and Kubrick — most famously Vertigo, Anatomy of a Murder, and Spartacus. Watanabe and his title designer explicitly cited the Bass aesthetic. The card-style character introductions referencing each crew member's name and bounty were the show's hallmark visual identity.

question: Hideaki Anno was a Gainax founding member from the 1981 Daicon III convention opening animation. Daicon was the Osaka science-fiction convention; Daicon III's now-famous opening was an animated short by college-student amateurs that became legendary in fan circles. The Daicon III opening features a young girl rendered in a style strongly reminiscent of which animator who would later be associated with Gainax?
answer: Hideaki Anno himself, with key animation from Hiroyuki Yamaga and Takami Akai
choices: Hideaki Anno himself, with key animation from Hiroyuki Yamaga and Takami Akai
Yoshiyuki Sadamoto, working from a Hayao Miyazaki story concept
Mahiro Maeda, with backgrounds painted by a young Yoshitaka Amano
Toshio Okada, working with college students from Osaka University of Arts
context: The Daicon III opening, made in 1981, was extended into the Daicon IV opening in 1983. Both shorts became legendary in fandom and are credited with directly leading to the formation of Gainax in 1984. Hiroyuki Yamaga, Hideaki Anno, Toshio Okada, and Takami Akai were the founding partners. The shorts' rights have long been disputed because they used unlicensed character cameos.

question: Studio Ghibli's relationship with Disney's North American distribution began with a 1996 deal brokered by producer Toshio Suzuki and the Walt Disney Company. The deal granted Disney non-exclusive distribution rights for most Ghibli films through 2017 with one notable exception. Which Ghibli film was excluded from Disney's distribution rights?
answer: Grave of the Fireflies, which was distributed in the US by Sentai Filmworks and Central Park Media
choices: Grave of the Fireflies, which was distributed in the US by Sentai Filmworks and Central Park Media
Castle in the Sky, distributed by Warner Brothers under its Streamline Pictures branch
Whisper of the Heart, distributed independently by Bandai Visual through TriStar
Princess Mononoke, distributed by Miramax Films alongside The Wind Rises
context: Grave of the Fireflies was produced not by Ghibli but by Shinchosha, with Ghibli only providing the animation. The film's licensing was therefore separate. Sentai Filmworks reissued the film in 2012 with a new dub. Disney distributed nearly every other Ghibli theatrical release in North America from 1997 through 2017, when the deal lapsed and GKIDS took over.

question: Akira's American theatrical release came on December 25, 1989 through Streamline Pictures, with an English-language dub that became the de facto US version for over a decade. The 2001 Pioneer Entertainment re-release with a new dub had which famous voice actor in the role of Kaneda?
context: Joshua Seth voiced Tetsuo in the 2001 dub. Bosch voiced Kaneda. The 1989 Streamline dub had Cam Clarke as Kaneda and Jan Rabson as Tetsuo. Steve Blum has said in interviews that he turned down a chance to audition for Kaneda in the Streamline dub because he was unsure how to play a teenage protagonist with that level of intensity.

question: Sailor Moon's 1992-1997 anime adaptation by Toei Animation famously had to navigate a complex syndication relationship in North America. The first English-language dub by DIC Entertainment in 1995 cut roughly six episodes and renamed almost every character. One particular character — a transgender man in the original Japanese sailor team — was rewritten by DIC as which kind of character?
answer: Two of the Sailor Starlights were rewritten as cisgender female cousins
choices: Two of the Sailor Starlights were rewritten as cisgender female cousins
Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune were rewritten as platonic cousins
Zoisite was rewritten from a male villain into a female villain
Sailor Saturn was rewritten as an unrelated cosmic entity rather than reborn Setsuna
context: DIC removed any romantic suggestion between Sailor Uranus and Sailor Neptune by recoding their relationship as cousins. The Sailor Starlights — male in civilian form, female as senshi — were never adapted into English by DIC because their gender presentation was deemed too complex. Viz Media's 2014 re-dub restored all original characterizations and relationships.

question: Studio Ghibli's distinctive watercolor-on-canvas background style — particularly evident in My Neighbor Totoro, Kiki's Delivery Service, and Spirited Away — was largely developed by which Ghibli art director, who painted backgrounds for nearly every Miyazaki feature until his death in 2007?
context: Oga's signature watercolor-and-poster-paint backgrounds became synonymous with the Ghibli look. He served as art director on most major Ghibli films from 1988 to 2008. Yoji Takeshige took over much of the art-direction work after Oga's semi-retirement and led the backgrounds for Howl's Moving Castle and Ponyo. Naoya Tanaka led the backgrounds for The Wind Rises.

question: Berserk's Eclipse arc was adapted into film in 2012-2013 as the Berserk Golden Age Arc trilogy, directed by Toshiyuki Kubooka and produced by Studio 4C. The trilogy's third film — covering the Eclipse itself — was titled Descent and released in February 2013. The 1997 OVA version of the same arc, by OLM, did NOT depict the Eclipse on screen because of which production constraint?
answer: The OVA was 25 episodes long but ended on a freeze-frame before the Eclipse to avoid graphic content for TV broadcast
choices: The OVA was 25 episodes long but ended on a freeze-frame before the Eclipse to avoid graphic content for TV broadcast
Kentaro Miura personally requested the Eclipse be omitted from the 1997 adaptation
The OVA studio OLM ran out of budget before reaching the Eclipse and shipped without it
Japanese broadcast standards in 1997 prohibited the Eclipse's specific visual depictions outright
context: The 1997 OVA's final episode ends with Griffith activating the Behelit and the rest of the Band of the Hawk staring in horror — the Eclipse itself is left off-screen. Studio 4C's 2012-2013 trilogy depicted the Eclipse in full. Miura was directly involved in supervising both adaptations. The 2016 Berserk TV series by Liden Films attempted to continue the story past the Eclipse but was widely criticized for its CGI.
